## ToastHost

```typescript
function ToastHost({ children }: { children: ReactNode })
```

Wrap the part of the app that raises toasts.

Renders the stack itself, so there is nothing to place and no way
to forget to place it.

## useToast

```typescript
function useToast(): ToastApi
```

Raise a toast.

Throws outside a `ToastHost` rather than returning a no-op.
A silent no-op here means a save that reports success by showing
nothing, which looks exactly like a save that did not happen.

**Also** [`ToastApi`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#toastapi).

## Banner

```typescript
function Banner({ tone = "neutral", onDismiss, children, className, ...rest }: BannerProps)
```

A condition that is still true.

Not a toast: a toast is about something that just happened and
goes away, a banner is about a state — offline, read-only, licence
expiring — and stays until the state does not.

**Also** [`BannerProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#bannerprops).

## useAnnounce

```typescript
function useAnnounce(): Announcer
```

A live region and the function that speaks into it.

Two regions are rendered, not one. A single region whose
`aria-live` value changes is unreliable: the attribute is read
when the region is observed, so flipping it at the same moment the
text changes races, and the announcement comes out at whichever
urgency the implementation noticed first.

**Also** [`Announcer`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#announcer).

## LiveRegion

```typescript
function LiveRegion({ children = "", urgency = "polite" }: LiveRegionProps)
```

The declarative form, for a value that already lives in state.

`<LiveRegion>{`${n} results`}</LiveRegion>` is the whole usage.
Mounted empty on the first render so the region exists before it
has anything to say — see note 1 above.

**Also** [`LiveRegionProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#liveregionprops).
